novel_mechanics_found: tu93 L6 is a deterministic multi-entity timing maze - by far the richest enemy ecology met today. Entities: (1) the player is a 9-ring with a 4-pixel core, moving 6px per action on a cell lattice; (2) c-colored PATROLLERS with an f-pixel direction flag, moving 1 cell per player-move on fixed lines: c1 patrols a 3-cell vertical (period 4 - verified over 16 ticks, no stalls) crossing the goal corridor every ODD tick; c2 patrols the full bottom row (period ~12) and GHOSTS THROUGH blocks; co-location with a patroller = instant death (verified twice, including the mover-mover swap case); (3) 8-colored CHARGER blocks with f-pixel fire-direction flags: entering a charger fire line triggers an instant lethal charge that also DISPLACES the charger to the impact cell (its remains then block the passage, marked with a b-pixel); some charger cells were found vacated mid-run and could be walked through, while touching a still-armed charger cell killed (the exact disarm/trigger rule was not fully pinned down - three deaths went to mapping it). The level is a two-lock door design: the goal corridor cell guarded by c1 is provably unreachable on a safe tick (the lattice is bipartite, so arrival parity is fixed and c1 occupies the cell on exactly that parity - a wait-verb would break it but ACTION5/6 are inert and blocked moves do not tick enemies), and the single alternative passage lies inside the up-chargers fire line with no safe disarm approach (flanked by a lethal armed charger on one side and an unreachable island on the other).
gotchas: CRITICAL: env.reset() is parity-poisoned on tu93 (registry gotcha confirmed relevant) - after any death/GAME_OVER, rebuild with a NEW env via arc.make() + fresh scorecard and replay the 93-label prefix; never chain resets.
The 93-label resolver prefix reaches L5 cleanly and deterministically (replayed 4x identically).

Enemies tick once per SUCCESSFUL player move only: ACTION5, ACTION6, and blocked moves do not advance them (blocked moves DO burn the row-63 meter, 64px per level). There is NO wait-verb - this is what makes the c1 parity lock unbreakable.

c1 (goal-corridor guard): vertical patrol, period 4, occupies the corridor crossing cell every odd tick; all paths from spawn to that cell have odd length (bipartite lattice) - do not attempt the direct crossing, it is a guaranteed swap/co-location death (died twice confirming).

Charger f-pixels show fire direction; fired/vacated charger cells are safely walkable; touching a still-armed charger cell can kill (died once); charge impacts leave a blocking remnant (8-block with b-pixel) at the impact cell - which can permanently seal the col-24 door.
c2 ghosts through 8-blocks on its patrol; use its position each tick when routing the bottom corridor.
The row-30 dead-end pair and the (30,30)/(24,30) nubs are reachable and safe; visiting them revealed the vacated-charger walkability but no switch behavior.

Hypotheses for a future attempt: (a) find the exact charger trigger/disarm rule (some cells vacated without an obvious trigger - candidate: line-entry from ANY cell on the full column including above, e.g. the col-42 shuffle at row 18 may have discharged the col-42 down-charger harmlessly - if TRUE, the col-24 down-charger can be pre-fired safely from 24r18... which is itself behind the parity lock, but check other levels/verbs); (b) verify whether the up-charger can be spent by luring c2... c2 ghosting does NOT trigger chargers per one observation; (c) look for a diagonal or repeat-press verb that moves 2 cells (parity breaker) - not found in ACTION1-6.
narrative: Replayed the banked 93-action prefix to L5 four times (deterministic). L6 is a two-lock timing maze: after fully mapping the entity ecology across three exploratory deaths (each followed by a fresh-env rebuild per the parity-poisoned-reset gotcha), the analysis closed both routes: the direct goal-corridor crossing is parity-locked by a period-4 patroller on a bipartite lattice with no wait-verb (proven over a 16-tick observation), and the sole bypass passage sits inside an armed up-chargers instant-kill fire line whose disarm approaches are themselves lethal or unreachable. Honest null: no new level; delivered a complete mechanical dossier (patrol periods, charger fire/displacement/remnant rules, ghost interactions, meter semantics) plus three concrete unlock hypotheses for the next attempt.
